issues.legal_issue: A later commercial-area restriction does not apply to a housing project approved and commenced under the earlier regime merely because the project was completed after the restriction took effect.
material_facts: The housing projects were approved by local authorities and construction commenced before April 1, 2005, when the new commercial-area restriction took effect.
Under the rules in force when the projects were approved, local authorities permitted commercial space in housing projects, and the projects met the conditions then applicable for the deduction.
The projects were completed after April 1, 2005, and did not meet the newly introduced limit on commercial space.
The Revenue challenged decisions allowing the deduction; the prospective operation of the amendment was not disputed.
issues.conclusion: The new commercial-area restriction does not apply to housing projects approved before March 31, 2005, even if completed on or after April 1, 2005. The assessees remain entitled to the deduction under the conditions applicable when their projects were approved, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 80IB(10)(d), inserted with effect from April 1, 2005, is prospective. The Court held that the restriction is inextricably linked to approval and construction of a housing project and cannot be imposed on projects approved under the earlier regime; applying it to those projects would unsettle accrued rights and could require compliance with conditions that were not contemplated when approval was obtained. Although the ordinary tax rule is to apply the law in force in the relevant assessment year, that rule may yield where the statute, expressly or by necessary implication, indicates otherwise: Reliance Jute and Industries Ltd. v. CIT. The Court also relied on the principles concerning accrued rights in CIT v. Shah Sadiq and Sons, and the approach to prospective operation discussed in CIT v. Vatika Township Pvt. Ltd.; it distinguished the general assessment-year rule reflected in CIT v. Gold Coin Health Food Pvt. Ltd. and Karimtharuvi Tea Estate Ltd. The Court’s acceptance of the interpretation of “housing project” in CIT v. Brahma Associates also formed part of the context: under the earlier regime, permitted commercial use did not by itself prevent a locally approved project from qualifying as a housing project.

rule.if: housing_project_tax_deduction_appeal and project_approved_before_new_restriction and project_started_before_new_restriction and prior_conditions_satisfied and restriction_added_after_approval and project_completed_after_restriction

predicates.housing_project_tax_deduction_appeal: A tax appeal concerns whether a developer may claim a deduction for profits from a housing project.
predicates.project_approved_before_new_restriction: A local authority approved the housing project before the commercial-area restriction took effect.
predicates.project_started_before_new_restriction: The developer began construction of the housing project before the commercial-area restriction took effect.
predicates.prior_conditions_satisfied: The housing project met the conditions applicable when it was approved.
predicates.restriction_added_after_approval: The commercial-area restriction was introduced after the local authority approved the housing project.
predicates.project_completed_after_restriction: The developer completed the housing project after the commercial-area restriction took effect.

issues.definition: When a developer’s deduction appeal concerns a project approved and begun under the earlier regime, meets that regime’s conditions, and is completed after a later commercial-area restriction takes effect, the later restriction does not apply.
